statement: Whenever reverse_odd_levels(root) returns a result r, let H be the maximum depth of a node in root. Then r has nodes exactly at depths 0 through H, with exactly 2^d nodes at each depth d, in the same left-to-right positions as root. For every d with 0 <= d <= H and every p with 0 <= p < 2^d, the value at depth d, left-to-right position p in r equals: (a) the value at depth d, position p in root when d is even; (b) the value at depth d, position 2^d - 1 - p in root when d is odd. At depth d, position p is the 0-based left-to-right index; equivalently it is the d-bit path from the root with L=0 and R=1.
preconditions: root is a non-null perfect binary tree: every node has either zero or two children and all leaves have the same depth. The number of nodes of root is between 1 and 2^14 - 1 inclusive (i.e., at most 16383). Every integer value v stored in root satisfies 0 <= v <= 100000. Levels/depths are 0-indexed: the root has depth 0, and the depth of any other node is one more than its parent's depth.
